intro.text: Regal Rexnord Corporation (NYSE: RRX) (“we,” “us,” “our” or the “Company”) and its associates around the world help create a better tomorrow by providing sustainable solutions that power, transmit and control motion. The Company’s electric motors and air moving subsystems provide the power to create motion. A portfolio of highly engineered power transmission components and subsystems efficiently transmits motion to power industrial applications. The Company's automation offering, comprised of controllers, drives, precision motors, and actuators, controls motion in applications ranging from factory automation to precision tools used in surgical applications. The Company is headquartered in Milwaukee, Wisconsin and has manufacturing, sales and service facilities worldwide.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: In 2025, 2024, and 2023, we had no customer that accounted for more than 10% of our consolidated net sales.
There were no customers that accounted for more than 10% of consolidated net sales in 2025, 2024 or 2023.
US net sales for 2025, 2024 and 2023 represented 62.8 %, 60.4 % and 61.4 % of total net sales, respectively.
China net sales for 2025, 2024 and 2023 represented 5.3 %, 5.4 %, and 6.5 % of total net sales, respectively.

We generally maintain a dual sourcing capability to ensure a reliable supply source for our customers, although in some cases we depend on a limited number of single source suppliers for certain specialty materials and components.
We depend on certain key suppliers, and any loss of those suppliers or their failure to meet commitments may adversely affect our business and results of operations.

Certain portions of our revenue depend on several significant customers and distributors, and any loss, cancellation or reduction of, or delay in, purchases by these customers or distributors may have a material adverse effect on our business.
Our success depends on our continued ability to develop and manage these relationships.
We rely on estimated forecasts to meet customers’ needs, and inaccuracies in such forecasts could materially adversely affect our business.
In some instances, we rely on estimated demand forecasts, based on input from our customers, to determine how much material to purchase and product to manufacture.

Our ability to make required payments of principal and interest on our debt levels will depend on our future performance, which, to a certain extent, is subject to general economic, financial, competitive and other factors that are beyond our control.
Further, the availability and terms of future financing may depend upon our ability to maintain or achieve certain credit ratings on our senior debt.
Worsening economic conditions could also affect the financial viability of our suppliers, some of which could be considered key suppliers.
The funded status of our defined benefit pension plans depends on such factors as asset returns, market interest rates, legislative changes and funding regulations.

While our Board maintains responsibility for oversight of all areas of risk management, it relies on our Audit Committee to address significant financial risk exposure we may face and the steps management has taken to monitor, control and report such exposures.

Management is authorized to effect purchases from time to time in the open market or through privately negotiated transactions and may enter into Rule 10b5-1 trading plans to enact purchases on behalf of the Company.
Our principal source of liquidity is cash flow provided by operating activities.

The preliminary fair value of Property, Plant, and Equipment was determined using either the cost approach, which relies on an estimate of replacement costs of the new assets and estimated accrued depreciation, or the market approach.
